label: PF Backlog 596
title: EDP-15: stored_objects + artifacts metadata; refactor artifact_store/registry behind ArtifactService; /artifacts API = authz + metadata + streaming
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

commits: C1a: artifacts + stored_objects migration with RLS

brief.problem: Artifact handling is split across store/registry with no metadata model or authz.
brief.what_adds: Unified ArtifactService with DB metadata, authz, streaming.
brief.why: Needed before lifecycle, signed URLs and enterprise sharing.

objective: Create stored_objects and artifacts metadata, refactor artifact_store/artifact_registry behind a unified ArtifactService, and expose /artifacts with authorization, metadata, and streaming.
acceptance_criteria: C1a: migration 0005_artifacts creates stored_objects(tenant_id,checksum PK) + artifacts(id,tenant_id,project_id,run_id,name,version,checksum,size,soft-delete) with FK + indexes; applied via pfmigrate (no auto-migrate)
C1a: both tables have RLS ENABLE+FORCE + a tenant_isolation policy (USING + WITH CHECK) matching 0003
C1b: ArtifactService implemented in Go (metadata in Postgres, bytes via the object store) with round-trip + checksum + RLS negative tests
C1c: /artifacts API in go/edpsvc (authorized metadata + streaming or signed URL) verified e2e
Evidence: schemacheck shows the new tables; RLS/isolation test; language-rule OK; precheck fast PASS
approach: EDP-15 slices C1a (migration) -> C1b (ArtifactService Go) -> C1c (/artifacts API). Decisions: identity = logical artifacts.id + content-addressed stored_objects.checksum(sha256); versioning = immutable append-only (monotonic version); signed-URL vs streaming chosen by ObjectStore Capabilities; retention deferred to EDP-16
verification: C1a applied via pfmigrate; schemacheck OK: expected 10 tables/11 indexes; live 11/27
language-rule OK; precheck fast PASS (37 gates)
risks: Behavioral drift during Python→Go cutover of artifact endpoints
Authz model not yet defined for artifact scoping
Large refactor risk in registry/store modules
rollback: Feature-flag routing back to Python artifact_store during migration window.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Introduce ArtifactService facade in Go over ObjectStore + metadata store; refactor existing core/artifact_store.py and core/artifact_registry.py behind it; add stored_objects/artifacts tables via BI-PF-1309 schema; harden /artifacts API with authz and streaming.
conflict_findings: /api/v1/artifacts endpoints currently served by Python core — coordinate cutover with BI-PF-1312 storage split
duplication_findings: core/artifact_registry.py and core/artifact_store.py already handle artifact tracking — refactor, not rebuild
analysis.rationale: Consolidates duplicated artifact handling behind one service; touches live APIs so needs an explicit compatibility plan.
assumptions: Existing /api/v1/artifacts contract must remain backward compatible during migration
BI-PF-1309 tables land before metadata wiring
risks: Behavioral drift during Python→Go cutover of artifact endpoints
Authz model not yet defined for artifact scoping
Large refactor risk in registry/store modules
missing_info: Migration window and deprecation policy for Python artifact code

context_review.reason: Refactor direction is clear but security and migration decisions are human-owned.
